raw_problem: Using the epsilon-delta definition of a limit, prove that lim_{x->2} (3x + 1) = 7.
Using the limit definition of the derivative, prove that d/dx(x^3) = 3x^2.
Using the epsilon-delta definition of continuity, prove that f(x) = x^2 is continuous at x = 3.
Prove that the sequence a_n = (2n+1)/(n+3) converges to 2.
Using the limit definition of the derivative, prove that d/dx(1/x) = -1/x^2 for x not equal to 0.
Prove that e^x >= 1 + x for all real numbers x.
Let f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 1. Prove that f has a critical point at x = 1 and determine, with proof, whether it is a local maximum or a local minimum.
Using the definition of the Riemann integral as a limit of Riemann sums, prove that the integral from 0 to 1 of x^2 dx equals 1/3.
Prove that the series sum_{n=1}^infinity (1/2)^n converges and that its sum equals 1.
